Seattle startup Chiplytics lands $4.5M to catch fake and flawed chips before they hit the market. Seattle-based Chiplytics raised $4.5 million and opened an East Coast inspection facility to help manufacturers catch fake or defective semiconductor chips and other electronics. The startup uses AI and robotics to test every individual component rather than relying on spot checks. Read More
